cerebral phosphorus (31P)-NMR spectroscopy is a valuable tool for investigating the metabolic state of the brain during and after perinatal asphyxia.

the development of an early diagnostic technique for the detection of cerebral metabolic derangement in newborn infants.
the development of an early noninvasive method of monitoring brain energy metabolism in infants with perinatal asphyxia.
the use of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopic methods to study cerebral energy metabolism in the newborn.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cerebral metabolic abnormalities are detectable by 31P NMR in infants with birth asphyxia and that the metabolic changes are associated with the clinical severity of the asphyxia and with neuro-developmental outcome.
PCr/Pi ratios in the first 9 days of life are a good indicator of prognosis and that the lower the ratio the worse the prognosis.
PCr/Pi ratio is a useful prognostic indicator in the early postasphyxial period, but that the value of the ratio is limited by the time of measurement and the degree of hypoxia.

the phosphorus (31P)-NMR technique is a powerful tool for investigating cerebral energy metabolism in vivo in the newborn infant.
cerebral metabolism in the asphyxicated infant is initially normal and then changes to become abnormal.
